proposals.title: A repeated diagram whole denotes a component or state key rather than an object

evidence.quote:
Met 55.121.11 is the closest readable technical-rendering comparator yet.  It
combines a water source, repeated lifting components, a driving animal, shafts
and wheels, and numerous compact marks beside parts.  The reverse is
especially informative: four parallel lifting bays sit under a shared drive,
showing that repeated visual units can be components or stages of one machine
rather than four independent named objects.

proposals.title: A figure-linked whole selects treatment mode rather than a person or material

evidence.quote:
1. q13 prose blocks should organize primarily by bath/pool installation or
   treatment episode, not one text label per drawn figure.
2. Figure pose and placement should covary with treatment mode—immersion,
   pouring, drinking, sweating, entry, or exit—more than with a fixed sequence
   of alchemical colors.
3. Independently recoverable flow direction should often be supply/drainage
   between bath levels, while only a minority of paths need form closed loops.

root_limits: GDT214 describes a readable external machine comparator, not Voynich stage/state labels.
The quoted GDT210 treatment-mode covariance is a prediction, not an observed association. No independent Voynich treatment label is supplied.

Lexical duplicate search and different design bytes do not establish scientific novelty. IDEA39 overlaps IDEA36/37 in cross-owner state/class covariance; IDEA40 overlaps IDEA36 but contrasts procedural mode with process/material state. Retain as related unreviewed variants pending explicit design-identity review.
A named object model need not assign a unique physical owner; homography, generic object names and shared component names remain outside a strict injective-name rival.
A successful physical mode/state association does not alone establish that the label denotes that role rather than a correlated object.
